source.title: DoWG Unleashed: An Efficient Universal Parameter-Free Gradient Descent Method
source.authors: Ahmed Khaled; Konstantin Mishchenko; Chi Jin

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including supplementary material; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains VGG11 and ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10 with DoWG and reports training-accuracy curves, bearing on whether gradient-based training reaches low training error. It does not directly study the claim’s central size, label-corruption, or convergence conditions.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 training-accuracy curves in Figure 4 bear on V1 but provide no numeric values or textual description of the training-error outcome. Theoretical convex-optimization results and citations to edge-of-stability work do not test the other versions. Test-accuracy and step-size curves do not measure the claim’s training-error outcome.
record.test_reason: The experiments evaluate the proposed optimizer's performance. R1 and R2 concern DoWG, whereas V1 specifies SGD or Adam. The Adam comparator is declared in rows_left_out, but its training-error outcome cannot be read from the supplied text. The edge-of-stability experiments use adaptive stepsizes on linear regression, rather than the neural-network dynamics specified by V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the practical experiments but omits the central theoretical conclusion: DoWG matches tuned gradient descent's convergence rates up to logarithmic factors for constrained convex smooth and nonsmooth optimization without stepsize tuning. The authors also report edge-of-stability behavior on linear regression and competitive neural-network performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates its proposed adaptive DoWG optimizer on CIFAR-10 rather than reproducing the original training recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture (VGG11 versus ResNet-50) and iterate averaging are reported as relevant experimental distinctions; the authors state DoWG is less stable on ResNet-50 and that its averaged iterate often has better test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: DoWG's last iterate has worse test accuracy than Adam, while its averaged iterate often performs better; DoWG is less stable on ResNet-50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice and iterate averaging affect CIFAR-10 test performance and training stability.

fits_no_version.finding: NGD and DoWG show nonmonotonic suboptimality and effective stepsizes near 2/L on regularized linear regression; their adaptive stepsizes decrease after overshooting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive stepsizes can self-stabilize near the stability boundary on convex linear-regression objectives.

record.problems: The relevant training-accuracy results are shown only in plots, with no numeric values or textual description of whether training error approaches zero. Results are averaged over 8 random seeds; per-seed outcomes are not reported in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Training-accuracy curves for the other optimizers in Figure 4 were not extracted because the rows above record the proposed DoWG method’s results relevant to V1; the text does not give separate training-accuracy outcomes for those comparators.

untested.parts: No readable SGD/Adam training-classification-error outcome establishes or contradicts near-zero error. CIFAR-100, label corruption, size dependence, early stopping and regularization comparisons are untested.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies and extra-neuron comparisons.
Controlled depth comparisons, identity-shortcut comparisons and the specified initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and trainable depth.
Neural-network recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, sharpness growth toward the threshold and divergence from initially subthreshold rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons and normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 4's training-accuracy axes are identifiable, but curve endpoints and optimizer-specific outcomes are unavailable in the supplied text. Axis ticks alone cannot establish near-zero training error. Comparator curves are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller-model comparisons, early stopping, and the listed optimizer and training recipes beyond those shown in Figure 4.
